title: CAD to GIS and Ain el Abd to KSA-GRF17 transformation, a Riyadh block

headline.label: shift between the correct transformation and a relabelled code

service.name: CAD to GIS Conversion and Coordinate Transformation

data: No open CAD drawing exists, so we made a stand-in: an OpenStreetMap extract (roads, buildings and land use in a 920 × 786 m box near Kingdom Centre, Riyadh) exported to a layered DXF in Ain el Abd / UTM 38N (EPSG:20438) with operation EPSG:1111 (stated accuracy 18 m).
method: Export the stand-in to DXF: one layer per road class and land use, one building layer, street names as text.
Read the DXF with ezdxf, turn each closed polyline into its own polygon, and take the class from the layer name.
Join 89 street-name texts to the nearest road line, and compute length, area and geometry validity.
Transform to KSA-GRF17 / UTM 38N (EPSG:9358) with the pyproj operation Ain el Abd to KSA-GRF17 (1) (EPSG:9362).
limits: The DXF is a clean stand-in made from OpenStreetMap, so it does not show the problems of real CAD drawings such as unclosed polylines, blocks and mixed layers. A closed polyline inside another is read as a separate polygon, not a hole; that is right here because the source has no holes, and may be wrong for another drawing. The more accurate operation EPSG:9363 (ARAMCO grid, 5 to 10 cm) is not available to pyproj on this machine, so the result is good to about 2 m.
